original_value: This paper discusses the performance of a terrestrial radar interferometer for the structural monitoring of ancient masonry towers. High-speed radar interferometry is an innovative and powerful remote sensing technique for the dynamic monitoring of large structures since it is contactless, non-destructive, and able to measure fast displacements on the order of tenths of millimeters. This methodology was tested on a masonry tower of great historical interest, the Saint Prospero bell tower (Northern Italy). To evaluate the quality of the results, data collected from the interferometer were compared and validated with those provided by two types of accelerometer-based measuring systems directly installed on the tower. Dynamic tests were conducted in operational conditions as well as during a bell concert. The first aimed at characterizing the dynamic behavior of the tower, while the second allowed to evaluate the bell swinging effects. Results showed a good agreement among the different measuring systems and demonstrated the potential of the radar interferometry for the dynamic monitoring of structures, with special focus on the need for an accurate design of the geometric aspects of the surveys.

result.paraphrase: This paper examines how well a terrestrial radar interferometer performs in monitoring the structural condition of ancient masonry towers. High-speed radar interferometry is an innovative and powerful remote sensing method for dynamic monitoring of large structures because it is contactless, non-destructive, and capable of measuring rapid displacements on the order of tenths of millimeters. The method was applied to the Saint Prospero bell tower, a masonry tower of major historical interest in Northern Italy. To assess result quality, interferometer data were compared with and validated against measurements from two accelerometer-based systems installed directly on the tower. Dynamic tests were carried out under normal operating conditions and during a bell concert: the first to characterize the tower’s dynamic behavior, the second to evaluate the effects of bell swinging. The results showed good agreement across the different measuring systems and confirmed the promise of radar interferometry for structural dynamic monitoring, with particular emphasis on the importance of carefully designing the survey geometry.
